claims.publicWording: SkillNet turns company documents into courses that employees can work through.
limitations: The public site does not yet include a live product demo.
Generated material still belongs in a human review workflow.

claims.publicWording: Admins manage training content and employees learn, practise and build a progress record in separate product workflows.
limitations: This statement describes the company-first product baseline, not a hosted service.
The provisional site does not claim outcome improvements or adoption metrics.

claims.publicWording: SkillNet is open-source software designed to be self-hosted as one instance per company.
limitations: Installation and infrastructure remain the operator's responsibility.
This site does not offer a managed cloud service.

claims.publicWording: AI agents can propose a course structure and learning material, while people remain in the review path before content reaches learners.
limitations: The quality of generated material still depends on the sources, configuration and human review.
SkillNet does not transfer accountability for training decisions to an AI model.

claims.publicWording: Courses combine structured modules, exercises and evaluation so a learner can practise rather than only consume generated content.
limitations: No improvement in learning outcomes is claimed without measured evidence.
The public site does not yet provide a live product walkthrough.

claims.publicWording: SkillNet is being designed so the same trusted knowledge can produce different explanations, practice and interfaces as each learner's context changes.
limitations: This is the product direction, not a claim that full adaptive regeneration is available today.
Adaptation must remain traceable to shared sources, objectives and criteria.
